source_meta._title: The game freezes while doing a world backup

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition using the integrated single-player world-selection interface. Run the exact first affected version, Minecraft 1.13. The report states that the problem is not exclusive to a particular operating system or hardware configuration. Use a pre-existing large local world save: the original reporter used the approximately 18 GB Białowieża Forest showcase map and also reproduced with a world of approximately 460 MB on an SSD.
preconditions: Install or create a launcher installation for the exact affected version Minecraft 1.13; do not use the listed fix version 26.1 Snapshot 6.

Place a pre-existing large Java Edition world in the Minecraft saves directory so that it appears on the Singleplayer world list. Prefer the approximately 18 GB Białowieża Forest map used by the reporter if it is already available; otherwise use the largest compatible world available. The smallest reliably affected size is not established.
Do not create a new empty world for this test, because the report states that reproduction depends on world size and that smaller worlds may not produce the condition.

Ensure the storage device holding the Minecraft game directory has enough free space for an additional backup copy of the selected world. For the reporter's approximately 18 GB world, allow at least that much additional space plus a safety margin.
Close the target world if it is currently loaded. The reproduction begins from the Minecraft title screen and uses the world-management UI rather than the in-world pause menu.

Use the report's simpler normal-backup route, Edit World -> Make Backup. The alternative Optimize World route specifically requires a large 1.12 world and an additional conversion process, but is not necessary to trigger the backup operation described by the report.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for the exact version Minecraft 1.13 and start the game. Do not select a newer affected version or the fix version for this primary reproduction attempt.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.13 title screen is displayed and its menu buttons respond to input.

steps.action: From the title screen, open the local single-player world list by moving the pointer over the Singleplayer button and pressing the default primary mouse button, left-click.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is displayed and the pre-existing large test world appears in the world list.

steps.action: Select the large test world by left-clicking its entry once. Use the approximately 18 GB Białowieża Forest showcase world if available; otherwise select the largest compatible existing world available, preferably at least approximately 460 MB. Do not double-click, because that would load the world instead of preparing it for editing.
steps.success_cue: The intended large world's row is visibly highlighted on the Select World screen, and the Edit button is enabled.

steps.action: Open the selected world's management screen by left-clicking the Edit button. Do not click Play Selected World.
steps.success_cue: The Edit World screen for the selected large world is displayed, including the Make Backup button.

steps.action: Confirm that the screen belongs to the intended large world by checking the displayed world name. Do not rename, reset the icon, optimize, or otherwise modify the world during this route.
steps.success_cue: The intended large world remains selected and the Make Backup button is ready to be activated.

steps.action: Initiate exactly one normal world backup by left-clicking the Make Backup button once. Do not repeatedly click, press Escape, close Minecraft, or start another operation after issuing this input.
steps.success_cue: The Make Backup input has been issued for the selected large world and the backup-copy operation has just begun; immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without further interaction.

stor.handoff_condition: The Make Backup button has just been activated once for the selected large world in Minecraft 1.13. Leave the client untouched while the backup proceeds and begin observing client responsiveness and backup progression.
uncertainties: The report does not establish a universal minimum world size. The reporter initially used an approximately 18 GB world and later reproduced with a world of approximately 460 MB on an SSD, while also stating that smaller worlds were not affected. The threshold may therefore vary by machine and storage performance.

The supplied report identifies the Białowieża Forest showcase map but does not include the map itself or a current download location. The executor must already have that map or another sufficiently large compatible world.

The first affected version, Minecraft 1.13, is selected as required. The report's alternative Optimize World route would require opening a large 1.12 world in this version and selecting Backup and Load; this plan instead uses the simpler independently reported Edit World -> Make Backup route.

The report's environment field was removed because the condition was not considered environmentally exclusive. No specific operating system, CPU, memory allocation, graphics mode, or storage type is required by the supplied evidence.

A reported size of approximately 460 MB reproduced on the reporter's system but is not guaranteed to reproduce on faster hardware. If one backup completes too quickly for meaningful observation, repeat the plan with a larger existing world rather than repeatedly backing up the same small world.

source_meta._title: The prevention of fall damage from wind charges is not retained upon reloading the world

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w14a in a single-player world (integrated server), with commands/cheats available. Use a temporary Creative-mode setup, then perform both trials in Survival mode. The test site should have a level, solid landing surface and unobstructed open sky above it.
preconditions: Launch the world specifically in Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w14a, not the listed fix version.
Use a single-player world in which commands are permitted so that command blocks can be obtained and the player can be switched to Survival mode.
Only one player should be present, ensuring that both @p selectors target the reproducing player.
Prepare a level, solid landing surface with open sky and no overhead blocks that could interrupt the launch or descent.
The player must have full health before the control trial and again before the reload trial.
Use the same world and the same command-block apparatus for the control trial and the reload trial.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the 24w14a installation and open or create a single-player test world. For the simplest setup, create the world in Creative mode with commands allowed; the player will be switched to Survival before testing.
steps.success_cue: The player is inside a world whose active game version is 24w14a and can execute commands.

steps.action: Move to a level area made of solid blocks with unobstructed open sky. Leave enough horizontal room for two adjacent command blocks and enough space beside them for the player to stand and reach a button.
steps.success_cue: A flat landing surface and a clear vertical launch path are available at the test site.

steps.action: Press T to open chat, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter to obtain an impulse command block.
steps.success_cue: An orange impulse command block is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press T, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter to obtain a chain command block.
steps.success_cue: A green chain command block is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press T, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter to obtain a button for activating the impulse command block.
steps.success_cue: A stone button is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Select the impulse command block in the hotbar and right-click the landing surface to place it. Orient it so that its arrow texture points horizontally toward an adjacent empty block position. If necessary, break and replace it until the arrow has the required direction.
steps.success_cue: The impulse command block is placed, and its arrow points into an empty adjacent position where the chain command block can be placed.

steps.action: Select the chain command block and place it directly in the adjacent position into which the impulse command block's arrow points. Orient the chain block along the same line, with its arrow pointing away from the impulse block.
steps.success_cue: The two command blocks are adjacent, and the impulse block's arrow points directly into the chain block.

steps.action: Right-click the impulse command block to open its configuration screen. Set its block type to Impulse, condition to Unconditional, and redstone mode to Needs Redstone. Enter the report's command in the command input without a leading slash, then select Done.
steps.success_cue: The impulse command block is configured as Impulse, Unconditional, Needs Redstone, and displays the exact wind-charge summon command.

steps.action: Right-click the chain command block to open its configuration screen. Set its block type to Chain, condition to Unconditional, and redstone mode to Always Active. Enter the report's command in the command input without a leading slash, then select Done.
steps.success_cue: The chain command block is configured as Chain, Unconditional, Always Active, and displays the exact levitation command.

steps.action: Select the stone button and right-click an accessible face of the impulse command block to attach it. Do not place the button between the impulse and chain command blocks.
steps.success_cue: A reachable button is attached to the impulse command block while the impulse block still points directly into the chain block.

steps.action: Stand on the level landing surface next to the apparatus, close enough to right-click the button. Ensure the player is the only player in the world, has open sky above, and will land on the same level surface from which the wind charge is summoned.
steps.success_cue: The player is within reach of the button, is the nearest and only player for both @p selectors, and has an unobstructed vertical path above the level landing area.

steps.action: Press T, enter the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter to switch the player to Survival mode.
steps.success_cue: The Survival HUD is visible, including hearts and hunger icons, and the player can take normal fall damage.

steps.action: Before the control trial, verify that all ten hearts are filled, the Levitation status icon is absent, and the player is standing on the prepared landing surface. If health is not full, remain at full hunger and wait for natural regeneration before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Survival mode at full health, has no active Levitation effect, and is standing at the test point.

steps.action: Perform the no-reload control trial by right-clicking the button once. Keep the game open and do not exit the world during this trial.
steps.success_cue: The player is propelled upward and receives the short Levitation effect, confirming that the impulse command and its chained command both executed.

steps.action: Do not deliberately move onto a different-height landing surface. Allow the Levitation effect to expire and wait until the player has landed back on the prepared level surface.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the level landing surface again and the Levitation status icon has disappeared.

steps.action: Use the first launch only as the report's control check. Confirm that this no-reload trial completed without reducing the player's health. If health was reduced, discard that trial because the report notes an intermittent unrelated failure; regenerate to full health, return to the same test point, and repeat steps 14 through 16 before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: A no-reload control launch has completed without health loss, and the player is ready to reset for the reload trial.

steps.action: Return to the exact test position within reach of the button. Wait until all ten hearts are filled and the Levitation effect is absent. Do not change the command-block configuration or the landing surface between trials.
steps.success_cue: The player is again in Survival mode at full health, standing at the same test point with no Levitation effect active.

steps.action: Begin the reload trial by right-clicking the button a second time. Do not wait for the player to reach the top of the launch.
steps.success_cue: The player has started moving upward and the Levitation effect is active.

steps.action: As soon as upward movement is visibly underway, press Esc to pause the single-player world. Do this promptly while the player is still rising, rather than near the apex or during the descent.
steps.success_cue: The pause menu is open while the player is still airborne early in the launch.

steps.action: From the pause menu, select Save and Quit to Title. Because the integrated single-player world is paused while the menu is open, select this after confirming that the pause menu was opened early in the ascent.
steps.success_cue: The world has closed and the Minecraft title screen is displayed.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer and highlight the same saved world used for the command-block setup. Do not create a new world.
steps.success_cue: The original 24w14a test world is selected in the world list.

steps.action: Select Play Selected World to re-enter the same world. As soon as the playable world view appears, provide no movement input and immediately hand control to the observation subsystem. The player must still be airborne with enough descent time remaining for the approximately two-second login damage-immunity period mentioned by the report to expire before landing.
steps.success_cue: The same world has finished loading to a playable view, and the Survival player is still airborne above the prepared landing surface rather than already standing on it.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just re-entered the same 24w14a world and is still airborne above the original level landing surface after the second wind-charge launch. The game is unpaused, no movement input is being supplied, and sufficient airborne time should remain for the post-login damage-immunity period to expire before landing. Begin observation immediately and continue through the landing.
uncertainties: The report does not specify the command blocks' redstone modes. Setting the impulse block to Needs Redstone and the chain block to Always Active is a practical configuration that allows one button press to execute both supplied commands in sequence.

The report does not specify exact block coordinates or apparatus geometry. A level solid surface with open sky is used so that the player can return to the same Y-level as the wind-charge explosion without obstruction.

The report provides no exact maximum delay between pressing the second button and exiting. The executor must pause and save very early in the ascent; if the player has already reached the apex or begun descending, reset to full health and repeat the reload trial.

The report warns that another unidentified issue can sometimes cause damage even during the no-reload control trial. A trial that fails this control must be discarded rather than used as the reload reproduction.

The remaining airborne time after re-entry cannot be guaranteed from a fixed delay because world-loading duration and the precise exit moment can vary. The required readiness cue is that the player is still clearly airborne when the playable view returns.

source_meta._title: Trader llama inventory shifted, partially lost during upgrade

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition, single-player/integrated server. Create the save in the exact release 1.20.4, then open that same save in the affected release 1.20.5. Use clean vanilla client profiles that share the same saves directory. Creative mode and enabled commands are practical choices for executing the report's supplied summon command deterministically.
preconditions: Install or configure launcher profiles for the exact Java Edition releases 1.20.4 and 1.20.5.
Ensure both launcher profiles use the same game directory, or otherwise ensure the 1.20.4 world remains available unchanged to the 1.20.5 profile.
Use a temporary test world. Do not perform this upgrade on an important world without a backup.
Run without mods, third-party server software, or datapacks that alter entities, inventories, or data conversion.

Use keyboard-and-mouse controls or equivalent rebound controls. Default relevant inputs are T for chat, E for inventory, Esc for pause/closing a screen, right-click for Use/Interact, and Left Shift for Sneak/Dismount.
Do not create the test world directly in 1.20.5; the same save must first contain the configured trader llama while saved by 1.20.4.
The supplied attachment world is not required because the report explicitly provides a summon-command route that skips manual summoning, taming, and chest equipping.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation whose version is exactly Java Edition 1.20.4, then launch it. Do not begin with 1.20.5.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 1.20.4.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer -> Create New World. Give the world a recognizable name such as "MC-271109 upgrade test", set Game Mode to Creative, enable Allow Cheats/Allow Commands, leave the seed and other generation settings at their defaults, and create the world.
steps.success_cue: A new 1.20.4 world begins loading with commands enabled.

steps.action: Wait after entering the world until nearby terrain has rendered and movement and camera controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Overworld, surrounding chunks are visible, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: On level ground, construct a temporary enclosure with at least a 5-by-5-block clear interior and a two-full-block-high perimeter made from solid blocks. Leave the top open and stand near the center of the enclosure. This keeps the trader llama near the player across the save-and-upgrade sequence.
steps.success_cue: The player is inside a clear enclosure whose perimeter is two blocks high, with enough room to summon and mount a llama.

steps.action: Press T, or the rebound Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is visible and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, capitalization of NBT field names, item identifiers, slot numbers, commas, braces, and brackets. Press Enter once to execute it. Do not modernize or otherwise modify the command.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback indicates that a Trader Llama was summoned, and one trader llama is visible inside the enclosure near the player's former position.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so that the main hand holds no usable item. Move within interaction range, center the crosshair on the trader llama, and right-click it once to mount it.
steps.success_cue: The viewpoint changes to the mounted position on the trader llama and the player remains seated on it.

steps.action: While mounted, press E, or the rebound Open Inventory control, to open the trader llama's inventory rather than the player's normal inventory.
steps.success_cue: A llama inventory interface is visible, including the llama equipment area and the storage slots supplied by its chest.

steps.action: Without clicking, shift-clicking, dragging, or otherwise moving any item, verify the pre-upgrade setup: the llama's chest storage contains one egg, one fern, and one dirt stack. The exact number of additional empty storage slots may vary; only the three supplied item stacks are required.
steps.success_cue: The egg, fern, and dirt are all simultaneously visible in the trader llama's chest-storage interface before upgrading.

steps.action: Press Esc to close the llama inventory without moving any item.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible again and the player is still mounted on the trader llama.

steps.action: Press Left Shift, or the rebound Sneak/Dismount control, once to dismount. Do not attack or otherwise interact with the llama afterward.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing beside the same trader llama inside the enclosure.

steps.action: Press Esc and select Save and Quit to Title. Wait for the title screen; do not force-close the game while the world is saving.
steps.success_cue: The 1.20.4 title screen has returned, indicating that the world was closed and saved.

steps.action: Create a safety backup of the saved world: open Singleplayer, select "MC-271109 upgrade test", choose Edit, then choose Make Backup. Wait for backup completion and return to the title screen. Continue the reproduction with the original world, not by restoring or opening the backup. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AThings_not_to_do?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Minecraft reports that the backup was created, and the original test world remains listed in Singleplayer.

steps.action: Return to the title screen, select Quit Game, and wait until the 1.20.4 game process has fully closed before changing launcher versions.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft 1.20.4 is closed and the launcher is available.

steps.action: In the launcher, select or create an installation whose version is exactly Java Edition 1.20.5 and launch it.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 1.20.5.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, select the original world named "MC-271109 upgrade test", and choose Play Selected World. Do not use Re-Create and do not make a new 1.20.5 world. If Minecraft displays an upgrade or backup warning, choose the option that creates a backup and then loads the selected world; otherwise continue loading normally.
steps.success_cue: The original world begins loading under Java Edition 1.20.5.

steps.action: Wait for the upgrade and world load to finish. Do not interact with the trader llama until surrounding chunks have rendered and player movement responds normally. If needed, briefly press F3 and verify that the debug overlay identifies the running client as 1.20.5, then close the overlay with F3. Locate the same trader llama inside the enclosure.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the converted world under 1.20.5, movement is responsive, and the previously summoned trader llama is visible inside the enclosure.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot, center the crosshair on the same trader llama, and right-click once to mount it. Do not attack the llama and do not place or remove any items.
steps.success_cue: The player is mounted on the original trader llama in the upgraded 1.20.5 world.

steps.action: Press E, or the rebound Open Inventory control, once to open the upgraded trader llama's inventory. As soon as the interface appears, stop all input: do not click, shift-click, drag, add, or remove any item.
steps.success_cue: The upgraded trader llama inventory interface is open and stable, ready for the separate observation subsystem to record its slot contents.

stor.handoff_condition: The original world created and saved in 1.20.4 has been loaded by 1.20.5, the same trader llama is mounted, and its inventory interface has just been opened without any post-upgrade item manipulation. Begin inventory-state capture immediately while leaving every slot untouched.
uncertainties: The downloadable world attachment was not supplied as usable world data here. This plan therefore uses the exact summon command explicitly offered by the report as the alternative reproduction route.

The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, game mode, or terrain type. Creative mode, enabled commands, default world generation, and the temporary enclosure are practical execution choices rather than reported requirements.

The report does not specify the interaction sequence for opening the llama interface. Mounting the already-tamed trader llama and pressing the inventory control is used as the practical execution method.

The supplied summon command does not specify the llama's Strength value, so the inventory interface may contain more empty storage slots in some runs. The three relevant pre-upgrade stacks are still the egg, fern, and dirt assigned to NBT slots 2, 3, and 4.

The description and a comment also mention the trader llama carpet/decor slot, but the report's supplied command does not populate DecorItem. This reproduction plan preserves that command unchanged and exercises the three chest-storage items only.
External verification was used only for the optional safety-backup UI path; the report's version numbers, cross-version order, entity command, NBT, and item setup were preserved unchanged.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-296708:Data from the 'jukebox_playable' component doesn't carry over from older versions.
source_meta._title: All non-default jukebox_playable components are deleted from existing items when updating past 1.21.4

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition, local single-player world created and saved in 1.21.4, then opened from the same saves directory in release 1.21.5. Use an unmodified client and a disposable Creative-mode test world with commands enabled. The report does not require a particular seed, coordinates, multiplayer server, datapack, resource pack, or graphics setting.
preconditions: Install or configure launcher profiles for Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.4 and 1.21.5.
Ensure both launcher profiles use the same game directory so the world created in 1.21.4 is visible to 1.21.5.
Use a disposable test world because opening it in 1.21.5 upgrades its saved data. Do not later reopen the upgraded copy in 1.21.4.
Enable commands when creating the 1.21.4 world. Creative mode is selected for operational simplicity; the report does not state that a particular game mode is required.
Keep the command-created gravel item in the player's inventory throughout saving, closing, and upgrading the world. Do not place, drop, destroy, or otherwise replace it.
Do not use fix version 25w19a for this reproduction.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the exact Java Edition installation for release 1.21.4 and start the game. Do not start 1.21.5 yet.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is visible and identifies the running version as 1.21.4.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer and then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Name the world so it can be identified after changing versions. Set Game Mode to Creative and enable Allow Commands. No specific world seed is required, so leave the seed unset unless the execution environment requires one.
steps.success_cue: The configured world is named MC-296709-1.21.4-source, Creative mode is selected, and commands are enabled.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for world generation and player entry to finish. Do not continue while a loading screen is present.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the newly created 1.21.4 world, nearby terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is active and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's give command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Execute it in the in-game chat as the current player; do not modernize or otherwise alter the item or component syntax.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a syntax or permission error, command feedback reports that gravel was given to the current player, and a gravel item appears in the inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press E, or the currently bound Inventory control, and locate the newly given gravel item in the player's inventory or nine-slot hotbar. Leave the item there without moving it outside the inventory, dropping it, or placing it as a block. Close the inventory with E or Esc after confirming its presence.
steps.success_cue: A gravel item from the command is present in the player's saved inventory and has not been used, dropped, placed, or destroyed.

steps.action: Press Esc to open the pause menu, select Save and Quit to Title, and wait for saving to complete. Do not terminate the game process while the world is saving.
steps.success_cue: The 1.21.4 main menu is visible again, indicating that the world was closed through the normal save-and-quit path.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, select MC-296709-1.21.4-source once in the world list, and select Edit. Do not load the world again.
steps.success_cue: The edit screen for the correct 1.21.4 source world is open.

steps.action: Select Make Backup and wait until Minecraft reports that the backup has been created. This backup is only a safety copy; continue testing with the original world listed in Singleplayer.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft confirms that a backup of MC-296709-1.21.4-source was created and the backup operation has completed.

steps.action: Return to the main menu and select Quit Game. Wait until the 1.21.4 game process has closed completely before changing installations.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft 1.21.4 is no longer running and the launcher or desktop is visible.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the exact Java Edition installation for release 1.21.5. Confirm that this installation uses the same game directory as the 1.21.4 installation, and then select Play.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft 1.21.5 begins launching from the game directory containing the saved test world.

steps.action: Wait for startup to finish and verify the version shown on the Minecraft main menu before opening any world.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is visible and identifies the running version as 1.21.5.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer and select the original world named MC-296709-1.21.4-source. Do not select a newly generated world or the external backup copy.
steps.success_cue: The original world created and saved in 1.21.4 is highlighted in the 1.21.5 world list.

steps.action: Open the selected world in 1.21.5 by selecting Play Selected World or double-clicking the world entry. If Minecraft presents an upgrade or backup confirmation, choose the option that creates a backup if offered and then continues loading; do not cancel the opening operation. This opening operation is the data-version transition under test.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft proceeds past the world list or any upgrade confirmation and displays the world-loading screen for MC-296709-1.21.4-source.

steps.action: Wait until the upgraded world has fully loaded. Do not move, use, drop, place, clear, or replace the pre-existing gravel item after entry, and do not save and quit again before the observation subsystem takes control.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the same world under Minecraft 1.21.5, surrounding terrain is rendered, the loading screen is gone, and controls or menus respond normally.

stor.handoff_condition: The world originally saved in 1.21.4 has just been opened and allowed to finish loading in 1.21.5. The player is stationary, and the pre-upgrade gravel item has not been used, dropped, placed, cleared, or replaced. Hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect the saved item's components.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, game mode, inventory slot, or item-inspection method. A fresh Creative-mode world with commands enabled and an identifiable world name is used only to make the supplied command and cross-version world selection deterministic.

The report says that 1.21.5 or a newer snapshot can be used, but the formal affected-version list contains only 1.21.5 and 25w15a, while 25w19a is listed as the fix version. This plan therefore uses the first listed affected version, 1.21.5, and does not generalize the reproduction to later snapshots.

The safety-backup operation is not stated by the report; it is included because opening the world in 1.21.5 permanently upgrades saved data. The original selected world, not the backup archive, remains the test target.
No component-inspection command is added because the report does not prescribe one and inspection of the post-upgrade state belongs to the separate observation subsystem.

source_meta._title: Arrows lose their Punch enchantment property when unloaded

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft: Java Edition 14w26c in a local single-player world. Create the test structure in Creative mode with commands available, then change to Survival mode before firing either arrow. Use keyboard and mouse controls; the stated keys are defaults and should be replaced with the corresponding bound actions if controls have been changed.
preconditions: Configure and launch an isolated installation of exactly Minecraft: Java Edition 14w26c.
Create a new single-player Creative-mode world. No seed or coordinates are specified by the report.
Use an open, level area with a solid floor and enough horizontal room for the player to be moved without striking walls, falling from an edge, or entering hazards.
Keep commands available. A Creative single-player world in this version permits the item-give and game-mode commands used below.
Begin with full health. Do not equip armor or apply status effects unless they are already unavoidable, because the report does not specify them.
Preserve and reopen this same world when performing the logout/relogin portion of the reproduction.

steps.action: Launch the installation configured for Minecraft 14w26c, select Singleplayer, create a new Creative-mode world, and wait for initial world loading to finish.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded single-player world, nearby terrain is rendered, movement responds normally, and the player can fly and instantly break blocks.

steps.action: Move to a level, open area. Choose a section of floor with enough unobstructed space around it that neither arrow impact can push the player into a wall, drop, fire, water, or another entity.
steps.success_cue: A flat test area with several blocks of clear floor in every horizontal direction is available.

steps.action: Open in-game chat and execute the historical-version command that gives the nearest player one bow enchanted with Punch II. Include the leading slash because the command is being entered in game chat. This command uses the pre-1.13 item NBT form and numeric enchantment ID 49 for Punch.
steps.success_cue: A bow is added to the inventory. When the bow is inspected in the inventory, its tooltip lists Punch II.

steps.action: Open chat again and give the nearest player 64 arrows. Include the leading slash.
steps.success_cue: A stack of 64 arrows is visible in the player inventory.

steps.action: Open chat and give the nearest player eight dirt blocks for constructing the test structure. Include the leading slash.
steps.success_cue: At least eight dirt blocks are present in the player inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Move the Punch II bow into one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the inventory, leave the arrows anywhere in the inventory, and move the dirt into another hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E.
steps.exact_input: E; arrange bow and dirt in separate hotbar slots; E
steps.success_cue: The Punch II bow and dirt are accessible from separate hotbar slots, and the inventory contains arrows.

steps.action: Select the dirt hotbar slot. Enter Creative flight by double-tapping the Jump control, whose default key is Space, and rise slightly above the floor.
steps.exact_input: Select dirt; double-tap Space; hold Space briefly to rise
steps.success_cue: The player is flying in Creative mode with dirt selected in the active hotbar slot.

steps.action: Construct a vertical pillar exactly five dirt blocks tall, counting the first dirt block placed directly on top of the existing floor as block 1. Place four additional dirt blocks on top of it, producing blocks 1 through 5.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the floor once, then right-click the top face of the pillar four more times while rising as needed
steps.success_cue: A five-block-tall vertical dirt pillar stands on the floor.

steps.action: At the height of pillar block 5, attach one additional dirt block horizontally to a side face of block 5. The two highest dirt blocks must be directly beside each other at the same height.
steps.exact_input: Right-click a horizontal side face of the fifth/highest pillar block
steps.success_cue: Two adjacent dirt blocks form a horizontal pair at the top of the pillar.

steps.action: In Creative mode, break only the lower four blocks of the original vertical pillar. Leave the original fifth block and its horizontally adjacent block floating in place.
steps.exact_input: Left-click pillar blocks 1, 2, 3, and 4 once each; do not break either top block
steps.success_cue: Exactly two adjacent dirt blocks remain floating, with four complete empty block spaces between the floor and the underside of the pair.

steps.action: Return to the floor and stop flying. Inspect the structure from below. Designate one dirt block as the first target and the adjacent dirt block as the second target; retain this distinction for the rest of the procedure.
steps.exact_input: Descend with Left Shift, then double-tap Space to stop flying when at floor level
steps.success_cue: The player is safely standing on the floor, the two target blocks remain overhead, and the first and second target positions have been identified.

steps.action: Open chat and change the player to Survival mode using the historical numeric game-mode argument. Include the leading slash.
steps.success_cue: The Survival health and hunger bars are visible, blocks no longer break instantly, and Creative flight is unavailable.

steps.action: Select the Punch II bow in the active hotbar slot. Stand beneath the first target block, point the crosshair at the center of its underside, hold Use Item to draw the bow fully, and release Use Item to fire one arrow upward into the block. The default Use Item control is right mouse button.
steps.exact_input: Select Punch II bow; aim at first block underside; hold right mouse button until fully drawn; release
steps.success_cue: One arrow is visibly embedded in the underside of the first dirt block rather than lying on the floor or lodged in another surface.

steps.action: Move beneath the second target block without disturbing the first arrow. Aim at the center of the second block's underside, fully draw the same Punch II bow, and release to fire a second arrow upward.
steps.exact_input: Aim at second block underside; hold right mouse button until fully drawn; release
steps.success_cue: A second arrow is visibly embedded in the underside of the second dirt block, leaving one embedded arrow under each target block.

steps.action: Switch away from the bow to an empty hotbar slot or any slot that cannot fire another projectile. Confirm that both embedded arrows and both dirt blocks are still present.
steps.exact_input: Select a hotbar slot that does not contain the bow
steps.success_cue: The bow is not active, and two separate arrows remain embedded under the two adjacent dirt blocks.

steps.action: Stand directly below the first target so the embedded arrow is vertically above the player's body. Look at the first dirt block's underside and hold the Attack/Destroy control, whose default is left mouse button, until that dirt block breaks. Do not step aside as the arrow becomes unsupported.
steps.exact_input: Hold left mouse button on the first dirt block until it breaks
steps.success_cue: The first dirt block is gone and its embedded arrow is unsupported and falling toward the player; the second dirt block and second embedded arrow remain intact.

steps.action: Remain beneath the first arrow until it contacts the player. Do not evaluate or encode the distance of the resulting movement; continue once contact has occurred and the player is still alive. Allow only enough time for the player to land and regain normal movement control.
steps.exact_input: No movement input until arrow contact; then wait only until standing and movement are controllable
steps.success_cue: An arrow-contact cue has occurred, such as the hurt sound, damage animation, or health reduction, and the surviving player has regained normal control.

steps.action: Immediately unload the single-player world by opening the pause menu and selecting Save and Quit to Title. Do not create or enter a different world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is displayed and the test world is no longer running.

steps.action: Reopen the same saved world from the Singleplayer world list. Wait until terrain, the test structure, and entities have rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select the same test world -> Play Selected World
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the same Survival-mode world, the remaining dirt block has loaded, and its saved embedded arrow is visible beneath it.

steps.action: Keep the world unpaused and wait at least five real-time seconds before disturbing the remaining block. This allows the post-login player-invulnerability interval mentioned by the report to expire. Do not stand where the arrow could be released during this wait.
steps.exact_input: Wait at least 5 seconds with the world unpaused
steps.success_cue: At least five seconds have elapsed after loading and player movement continues to respond normally.

steps.action: Move directly beneath the remaining second dirt block. Align the player's body under the embedded arrow, select a non-bow hotbar slot, and aim the crosshair at the dirt block's underside.
steps.exact_input: Move beneath the second arrow; select a non-bow slot; aim at the remaining dirt block
steps.success_cue: The player is in Survival mode directly below the remaining embedded arrow, the login wait has elapsed, and the crosshair is on the supporting dirt block.

steps.action: Trigger the post-unload test by holding the Attack/Destroy control until the second dirt block breaks. Release the control and perform no further movement as the saved arrow becomes unsupported and falls toward the player.
steps.exact_input: Hold left mouse button on the remaining dirt block until it breaks, then release all controls
steps.success_cue: The second dirt block has just broken and the previously unloaded/reloaded arrow is now unsupported and falling toward or beginning to contact the stationary player.

stor.handoff_condition: The same world has been reopened, at least five unpaused seconds have elapsed, the player is in Survival mode directly beneath the second saved arrow, and the second supporting dirt block has just been removed. The arrow is now falling toward or beginning to contact the player; begin observation immediately without issuing additional player input.
uncertainties: The report provides no world seed, coordinates, difficulty, or exact terrain, so the plan uses a newly created flat local area as a practical setup choice.
The phrase 'four blocks space between the floor and the blocks' is interpreted as four complete air-block cells between the floor surface and the undersides of the two floating dirt blocks.

The report's displayed description commands use a newer item-NBT form and the later @s selector. For the recommended first affected version, the bow command is adapted from the historical syntax shown in Report Comment 3, changing only lvl:20s to lvl:2s so the required enchantment remains Punch II. Historical documentation also gives the old /give argument structure and Punch numeric ID 49. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Java%E7%89%881.7.2?utm_source=openai))

The five-second post-login delay is a conservative operational interpretation of the report's instruction to wait 'a few seconds.' A mechanics reference describes a 60-game-tick, three-second player spawn-invulnerability interval, but the exact historical implementation in 14w26c was not independently established. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/%E7%8E%A9%E5%AE%B6?variant=zh-tw&utm_source=openai))

Single-player Save and Quit is selected as the deterministic way to perform the report's example of unloading by logging out. The report does not state that a dedicated server or second player is required.

If the historical enchanted-bow command is rejected despite using 14w26c, stop rather than substituting modern Enchantments syntax; the exact launcher build and command error should be returned for version-specific resolution.
